overview: Player ESP is a wire-silent render overlay: on every Render3DEvent it walks mc.theWorld.loadedEntityList and draws a fixed translucent black box around every EntityPlayer except the local player. The entities it draws are fed by the server spawn stream (S0C for players, S0F for mobs, both filtered to EntityPlayer), and the drawing itself is pure client-side GL11 work, so the module has no packet fingerprint and no server-side detection surface.

sections.p: The module is a single Consumer<Render3DEvent> field carrying the @Handler marker that the client's PubSub bus subscribes at toggle time. The consumer loops mc.theWorld.loadedEntityList, skips the local player and any entity that is not an EntityPlayer, and calls RenderUtils.drawEsp(o, new Color(0, 0, 0, 21).getRGB()) for the rest. drawEsp renders a 1x2x1 axis-aligned box from (posX - 0.5, posY, posZ - 0.5) to (posX + 0.5, posY + 2.0, posZ + 0.5) using the color's alpha, so the box is a barely visible 8 percent opacity black outline at fixed size, with no color, health, distance or invisibility settings.

loadedEntityList is populated entirely from the receive path: S0C spawns players into the client world, S0F spawns mobs, and the destroy, teleport and velocity packets move and remove them. The EntityPlayer filter means only S0C-fed players ever render; S0F mob spawns are skipped by the instanceof check even though they populate the same list. The module reads entity positions each frame, so the boxes track interpolation and render through walls; nothing is sent back.

Rendering is client-local state. The module neither sends nor cancels any packet, and it does not mutate the entity list, so the server-side entity ledger is identical to a vanilla client's. There is no packet whose content could betray the overlay. The countering entries below are therefore honest boundaries: the checks that handle the S0C and S0F spawn stream in each anticheat, none of which can observe a render-side read of the same data.

files.label: ESP.java
files.explanation: The module: the Render3DEvent consumer, the loadedEntityList walk, the EntityPlayer filter and the fixed-color drawEsp call that make up the entire behavior. The @Handler field is the subscription contract with the PubSub bus.

files.label: RenderUtils.java (drawEsp)
files.explanation: The drawing utility the module calls: drawEsp builds a 1x2x1 box around the entity's feet position and hands it to the GL11 quad renderer in box(); the utility shows the fixed geometry and alpha blending that define the ESP's appearance.

countering.label: PacketEntityReplication (spawn ledger)
countering.explanation: Grim mirrors every spawn into a server-side entity ledger: the S0C and S0F handlers build PacketEntity objects with tracked positions and hitboxes that feed reach, phase and prediction checks, and a spawn also clears the player's accepted-spawn-teleport flag. This is the closest thing to a spawn consumer in the corpus, and it is a one-way mirror: the ESP reads the same spawn data locally for rendering, while the replication ledger records only server-originated state. Nothing the module does alters an entity's tracked position or existence, so the ledger sees a vanilla stream. The entry is the honest statement that entity-replication machinery cannot observe a render-only read.

countering.label: SetbackTeleportUtil (spawn teleport acceptance)
countering.explanation: The setback manager carries the spawn teleport acceptance flag (hasAcceptedSpawnTeleport) that gates teleport rejection and resync behavior after joins and respawns. The ESP moves nothing and sends no C03, so the acceptance state machine is driven purely by the server's own S08 and spawn traffic, exactly as for vanilla clients. The entry documents the other spawn-touching Grim surface and why a module that only draws boxes cannot reach it.

countering.label: MovingUtil (spawn-location bookkeeping)
countering.explanation: NCP's movement utilities touch the spawn data in one place: comparisons against the world spawn location (isSamePos against loc.getWorld().getSpawnLocation()) that feed the movement checks' world-state assumptions. The ESP produces no movement packets and mutates no world state, so every MovingUtil computation sees the same inputs as for a vanilla client. The entry is the honest gap for NCP's spawn story: its only spawn-adjacent logic is positional bookkeeping inside the movement layer, unreachable from a render module.

countering.label: LivingEntityIdLookup (spawn id cache)
countering.explanation: Photon caches entity id to type from the S0C and S0F spawn sends (WrapperPlayServerSpawnPlayer and SPAWN_LIVING_ENTITY) in a time-bounded cache so its packet-rewriting modules can classify entities later. It is a server-side mirror of exactly the spawn stream the ESP reads client-side. The module neither sends nor rewrites spawn traffic, so the cache contents are identical to vanilla. The entry states plainly that the only spawn-stream machinery in the corpus is a lookup cache, which has no opinion about what the client renders.
